welcome_page.title: Welcome to Your Experience With Motorcycle Travel
welcome_page.description:
This SmartUrbanity questionnaire asks about how you feel and what you experience while travelling by motorcycle or scooter. Your answers help identify barriers and opportunities for better urban mobility. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

questionnaire.title: 6. Your Experience With Motorcycle Travel

sections.title: Motorcycle and scooter use
sections.description: Questions about whether you ride a motorcycle, scooter or moped and how the road affects your riding.

questions.text: Do you ride a motorcycle, scooter or moped at least once a week to get to places? (E-scooters do not count here: they are covered in the cycling questionnaire.)
Why don't you ride a motorcycle or scooter, or why do you ride so rarely? (Select all that apply)
questions.help: We ask this to understand what limits the use of motorcycles and scooters for different people. Answering is optional, and you can also choose not to say.

options.text: I don't need to: other ways of getting around suit me better
I don't have a licence or a vehicle
It feels too dangerous in traffic
Poor road surfaces (potholes, cobblestones, tram tracks)
My health, a disability or my age makes it difficult

questions.text: How do traffic-calming features (e.g., speed bumps, rumble strips, road narrowings) affect your sense of safety while riding?
questions.help: Rumble strips are raised or grooved lines across the road that make vehicles vibrate. A road narrowing is a point where the carriageway is made narrower.

options.text: Make me feel much less safe
Make me feel slightly less safe

questions.text: How do parked cars or narrow lanes typically impact your ability to maneuver safely on your route?

options.text: No problem, I can handle these situations
Minor inconvenience, I adjust and manage
I have to maneuver with difficulty
I avoid these stretches of road

questions.text: How do road surface conditions (potholes, cobblestones, tram tracks) affect your riding?

options.text: They do not affect my riding
I slow down or change my line, but I feel safe
I avoid some roads because of their surface, even if the route is longer

questions.text: In the last 12 months, have you fallen or nearly fallen because of the road surface?

sections.title: Other road users, parking and charging
sections.description: Questions about other drivers, parking and charging for your vehicle.

questions.text: How confident are you in your ability to avoid crashes caused by “dooring” (car doors opening suddenly) or drivers failing to check blind spots?
questions.help: A blind spot is the area around a vehicle that the driver cannot see in the mirrors.

questions.text: To what extent does the behavior of other drivers (e.g., sudden lane changes, tailgating, or not yielding) affect your stress levels during a trip?
questions.help: Tailgating means following another vehicle at a very short distance.

options.text: Not stressful at all, it doesn't affect me
Slightly stressful, it occasionally bothers me
Moderately stressful, I notice it but manage
Very stressful, it frequently puts me on edge
Extremely stressful, it significantly affects my ability to ride safely

questions.text: How adequate are motorcycle-specific parking facilities in your city? Think about secure parking and designated spaces near destinations.
To what extent does the presence of charging stations (for electric motorcycles/scooters) influence your willingness to use your vehicle?

options.text: I don't have an electric vehicle, so this doesn't apply to me
